trust_decision.summary: UserService.GetUserByKey decides which user an API-key credential authenticates as; it first consults a single shared user cache that GetUserById/GetUserByOidc populate keyed by bare user ID, so a cache hit on a username (or any other cached key) is accepted as a valid API key and returned before any key or read_only check.

landing_point.why: Summary names the user caching service and a lookup resolved in the wrong context; GetUserByKey's cache.Get(key) is the API-key auth lookup that reads the shared cache.

fix_sites.entry_point: GetUserById: cookie auth, trusted-header auth, public user-param routes (middlewares/authenticate.go:212, middlewares/authenticate.go:184, routes/api/badge.go:46) prime the cache
same as above (cache write keyed by bare u.ID)
API key via Authorization Basic/Bearer header or ?api_key= query on every authenticated route (middlewares/authenticate.go:147, middlewares/authenticate.go:161)
same as above (main user api_key match, cache write)
same as above (additional api_keys table match, cache write)
FlushUserCache via Update/ResetApiKey/Delete/settings actions (services/user.go:297, services/user.go:333, routes/settings.go:464)

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: All changed sites are in services/user.go; the OIDC producer at services/user.go:195 sits in the same file, so it is not an out-of-scope module.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The cache hit at services/user.go:110-112 also returns before the requireFullAccessKey/read_only filter (repositories/api_key.go:33-35); a solver could argue read-only vs full-access keys are a separate authorization feature and the report is about username/API-key collision only.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Legitimate API-key lookups must still be served from cache (existing cache-hit test), read-only additional keys must keep working on non-heartbeat routes, and ResetApiKey/Update must still invalidate the old key; disabling the cache or keying without matching invalidation breaks one of these.

O6_input_shapes: user ID used as API key (GetUserById-primed entry)
header (Basic/Bearer base64) and ?api_key= query transports (both reach the same call)

O7_producer.where: services/user.go:101 and services/user.go:195 write *models.User into srv.cache keyed by bare user ID; services/user.go:249 and services/user.go:196 write other value types into the same cache

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Cache hit in GetUserByKey ignores requireFullAccessKey; the published fix keys by 'key_'+key only, so a read-only additional key cached by a non-heartbeat request is then accepted on the full-access heartbeat route.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Read-only key enforcement is a neighbouring feature (repositories/api_key.go:33-35, routes/api/heartbeat.go:40), not the username/key collision in the report.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file as landing point; filter lives in repositories/api_key.go (another package), route in routes/api

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Shared srv.cache also holds non-user values under unprefixed keys (OIDC 'provider_sub' -> user ID string, '<date>--active' -> []*User); the fix leaves the OIDC write unprefixed, so a provider named 'id' or 'key' collides with the new prefixes.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Requires an operator-chosen provider name; the value is a string, so the type assertion at services/user.go:93 would panic rather than authenticate.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: ApiKeyService.GetByUser caches []*ApiKey under bare userId in a cache whose invalidation matches keys by strings.Contains(key, userId) (services/api_key.go:97-103); a sibling cache lookup by raw key in this service would recreate the same collision.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The same maintainer pattern (bare-ID cache keys, shared cache) is already used there.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Add caching to GetUserByWebAuthnID / GetUserByResetToken (services/user.go:149-154) using the same srv.cache with unprefixed keys.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The comment at services/user.go:134 says caching was skipped only because the lookup is rare; adding it the same way as GetUserById is a natural optimisation.

O9_family: authentication bypass via cache-key confusion (type confusion of lookup context, CWE-843)

TestUserService_GetByKeyFromCache_Success at services/user_test.go:84) and middlewares/authenticate_test.go (WithFullAccessOnly at middlewares/authenticate_test.go:84); runs with sqlite/mocks, no external services needed

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Prefix the cache keys per lookup type ('id_'/'key_'), which is the published fix, and leave requireFullAccessKey and key revocation out of the cache key/invalidation.

out_of_scope_notes: After the published fix, deleting an additional API key (services/api_key.go:76-84, routes/settings.go:990) does not flush the UserService 'key_' entry, so a revoked key may stay valid up to the 1h cache TTL; not present at the pinned commit.
GetUserByOidc writes the sub->id mapping into srv.cache (services/user.go:196) while reading it from subjectCache (services/user.go:175), so the subject cache never hits; correctness bug only.
